case_title: Vipin Jaiswal v. State of A.P.
accused_occupation: Worked at a xerox cum type institute in Nampally (per PW1's evidence)
evidence_type: Oral testimony (PW1 father, PW2 cousin, PW4 mother, DW1 appellant); documentary (Ext. 019 chit)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.304B and 498A; sentence not stated in the judgment
high_court_outcome: Acquitted co-accused A2 and A3; maintained appellant's conviction under ss.304B and 498A
neutral_facts: The victim was married to the accused in February 1996. The victim's father alleged that after the marriage the victim was subjected to physical and mental torture by the accused and the accused's family for not getting sufficient dowry. Gold jewellery, silver items, furniture and other gifts were said to have been given at the marriage. On 2 April 1999 the victim's father went to the accused's house with relatives, and he alleged he was abused and physically pushed out. On 4 April 1999 the victim's father was told by telephone that the victim had suffered severe burn injuries and died at the accused's house. An FIR was lodged the same day and the police registered a case and investigated. At trial, the victim's father, the victim's cousin and the victim's mother testified. The father and mother stated that about six months after the marriage the victim reported that the accused had demanded Rs.50,000 to buy a computer for a business. The prosecution witnesses made general allegations of harassment but identified no specific acts of cruelty. The accused gave evidence that, while cleaning the house, he found a handwritten chit bearing the victim's handwriting and signature. The chit stated that nobody was responsible for the victim's death, that the victim's parents and family had harassed the accused, and that the victim was tired of life because of quarrels.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from burn injuries
financial_property_loss: Not applicable (alleged Rs.50,000 demand was not accepted as dowry; alleged marriage gifts worth above Rs.2,50,000 were not a loss found by the court)
motive: alleged: dowry demand of Rs.50,000 for purchasing a computer to start a business (not accepted as dowry by the court)
key_evidence_accepted: Appellant's testimony (DW1) and Ext. 019 suicide chit; evidence of PW1 and PW4 on the Rs.50,000 demand (found not to be dowry)
witness_credibility: Prosecution witnesses PW1 and PW4 gave only general allegations of harassment without specific acts; DW1's account of the chit was not rejected on proper grounds, the court found the lower courts' disbelief was based on imaginary reasoning
post_offence_conduct: Per DW1's evidence (not a court finding), he took the chit to the police station, which refused to receive it
custody_duration: Arrested; released on bail after about one month (per DW1's account); exact custody duration not stated
bail_history: Released on bail; bail bond discharged by the Supreme Court
trial_duration: offence: 4.4.1999; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 11.12.2006; Supreme Court: 13.03.2013
legal_representation: Appellant: A.T.M. Ranga Ramanujam, Prabhakar Sharma, Dipankar Das, Devesh Singh, Shanti Kumar Jaisani, Anu Gupta. State: Mayur R. Shah, D. Mahesh Babu, Suchitra Hrangkhawl, Amjid Maqbool, Amit K. Nain, M. Bala Shivudu
investigation_status: FIR registered on 4.4.1999; investigation completed; charge-sheet filed; trial held
procedural_irregularity: Neither the trial court nor the High Court compared handwriting under s.73 or sought expert opinion under s.45 Evidence Act on the chit
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.304B and 498A. High Court: appellant's conviction maintained; co-accused A2 and A3 acquitted. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, conviction set aside
prosecution_argument: The s.2 Dowry Prohibition Act phrase 'in connection with the marriage' covers the computer demand; PW1, PW2 and PW4 evidence proved dowry demands beyond Rs.50,000; the suicide note should not be believed as the victim was a matriculate; DW1's evidence alone cannot prove the note was written by the victim; cruelty soon before death was proved
defence_argument: The Rs.50,000 demand was for a computer for the accused's own business, not dowry; it is absent from the FIR; the suicide note (Ext. D19) is in the victim's handwriting and its signature matches Ext. D1
legal_principle_applied: Dowry requires a connection with the marriage; to convict under ss.304B and 498A the prosecution must prove beyond reasonable doubt cruelty or harassment soon before death; s.113B presumption depends on this; handwriting may be proved under ss.73 and 45 Evidence Act
precedent_relied_upon: Appasaheb & Anr. v. State of Maharashtra (2007) 9 SCC 721
other_sentence_order: Bail bond furnished by the appellant discharged
